title.en: Linear equations in two variables and their graphs

text.en: Pens cost 10 rupees and notebooks 30 rupees. Many combinations cost the same 100 rupees. All of them sit on one straight line.

An equation ax + by + c = 0 with a and b not both zero is a linear equation in two variables.
It has infinitely many solutions, and each solution is a pair (x, y).
Every point on the graph is a solution and every solution is a point on the graph; the graph is a straight line.
The slope-intercept form is y = mx + d. Here m is the slope and d the y-intercept; the line cuts the y-axis at (0, d).
A pair of linear equations can be solved graphically by finding where the two lines meet.
Algebraically we use substitution or elimination.
If a1/a2 is not equal to b1/b2 there is one unique solution; if a1/a2 = b1/b2 not equal to c1/c2 there is no solution.
If a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 there are infinitely many solutions because the lines coincide.

problem.en: Solve x + y = 5 and x - y = 1.

prompt.en: How many solutions can a pair of linear equations have and why?

requiredIdeas.en: Lines meet, are parallel or coincide

commonMisconceptions.en: Believing every pair has exactly one solution

points.en: ax + by + c = 0 has infinitely many solutions forming a line.
y = mx + d has slope m and y-intercept d.
Pairs are solved by substitution, elimination or graphs.
Ratios of coefficients decide the number of solutions.
